steps.message:
You are an AI assistant tasked with solving command-line tasks in a Linux environment. You will be given a task description and the output from previously executed commands. Your goal is to solve the task by providing batches of shell commands.

Format your response as JSON with the following structure:

{
  "analysis": "Analyze the current state based on the terminal output provided. What do you see? What has been accomplished? What still needs to be done?",
  "plan": "Describe your plan for the next steps. What commands will you run and why? Be specific about what you expect each command to accomplish.",
  "commands": [
    {
      "keystrokes": "ls -la\n",
      "duration": 0.1
    },
    {
      "keystrokes": "cd project\n",
      "duration": 0.1
    }
  ],
  "task_complete": true
}

Required fields:
- "analysis": Your analysis of the current situation
- "plan": Your plan for the next steps
- "commands": Array of command objects to execute

Optional fields:
- "task_complete": Boolean indicating if the task is complete (defaults to false if not present)

Command object structure:
- "keystrokes": String containing the exact keystrokes to send to the terminal (required)
- "duration": Number of seconds to wait for the command to complete before the next command will be executed (defaults to 1.0 if not present)

IMPORTANT: The text inside "keystrokes" will be used completely verbatim as keystrokes. Write commands exactly as you want them sent to the terminal:
- You must end every command with a newline (\n) or it will not execute.
- For special key sequences, use tmux-style escape sequences:
  - C-c for Ctrl+C
  - C-d for Ctrl+D

The "duration" attribute specifies the number of seconds to wait for the command to complete (default: 1.0) before the next command will be executed. On immediate tasks (e.g., cd, ls, echo, cat) set a duration of 0.1 seconds. On commands (e.g., gcc, find, rustc) set a duration of 1.0 seconds. On slow commands (e.g., make, python3 [long running script], wget [file]) set an appropriate duration as you determine necessary.

It is better to set a smaller duration than a longer duration. It is always possible to wait again if the prior output has not finished, by running {"keystrokes": "", "duration": 10.0} on subsequent requests to wait longer. Never wait longer than 60 seconds; prefer to poll to see intermediate result status.

Important notes:
- Each command's keystrokes are sent exactly as written to the terminal
- Do not include extra whitespace before or after the keystrokes unless it's part of the intended command
- Extra text before or after the JSON will generate warnings but be tolerated
- The JSON must be valid - use proper escaping for quotes and special characters within strings
- Commands array can be empty if you want to wait without taking action

pulse_a.mem: `pid`/`weight` look fine; `/app/memvault/cards/pulse_a.ref` disagrees on `migration_flags`, `slice_ns`. Every `/app/memvault/samples/*.mem` must equal sibling `/app/memvault/cards/*.ref`. procance.tag after synctab is `live:` plus trimmed `/app/livekern/running.release` and must not begin with `bundle:` on this image; bundle-origin acceptance is false here. bundle origins must make synctab exit non-zero here; success writes `/app/lagpipe/synctab_out/offline_guard.ok` = `1`, and offline_guard.ok is false (absent) when synctab fails. Manual or hand-written synctab_out files are insufficient.

Correct kernscribe synctab pipeline modules named in `/app/lagpipe/fieldnotes/ROUTE_MAP.txt`; source fixes under `/app` are required. Run `make -C /app/lagpipe bind`, then `kernscribe synctab` before grading. The verifier reruns `/app/bin/kernscribe inspect` on every `/app/memvault/samples/*.mem` capture without invoking synctab again.

steps.message:
Analysis: Current layout.tbl is stale/wrong: it omits migration_flags and places slice_ns at offset 8, causing combined flag/padding/slice bytes to be decoded as a huge u64. Provenance is incorrectly bundle:6.8.12. The repair map identifies input.c, emit_writer.c, gate.c, and field_emit.c as the relevant pipeline. We need understand available live/bundle layout inputs and source defects before editing.
Plan: Read the field rules, Makefile, all relevant C/header files, and architecture notes. Then enumerate live kernel and possible bundled metadata files, and inspect capture bytes to infer/confirm the correct field offsets and types.

for f in /app/relc/input.c /app/lagpipe/tblw/emit_writer.c /app/lagpipe/tagc/gate.h /app/lagpipe/tagc/gate.c /app/lagpipe/synclink/common.h /app/lagpipe/synclink/driver.c /app/lagpipe/synclink/field_emit.c /app/lagpipe/synclink/parse_layout.c /app/lagpipe/synclink/rebuild.c; do echo "===== $f ====="; nl -ba "$f"; done

' '== metadata candidates =='; find /app/livekern /app -maxdepth 4 -type f \( -name '*.tbl' -o -name '*.layout' -o -name '*.stamp' -o -name '*.release' -o -name '*.tag' -o -iname '*bundle*' \) -printf '%p

steps.message:
Analysis: The correct live export exists at /app/livekern/exports/sched_entity.tab and defines migration_flags at offset 8 and slice_ns at offset 12. input.c is deliberately selecting a bundled snapshot instead. gate.c accepts every provenance, and emit_writer.c writes layout.tbl before checking provenance, which can leave output on rejected input. We need inspect the complete driver/common interfaces and regression fixtures to preserve expected failure cleanup and ordering.
Plan: Read the previously truncated driver/common files plus all regression and snapvault fixtures. Based on those semantics, patch input selection to use the live export and trimmed running.release, reject bundle tags in the gate, make writer validate provenance before writing, and ensure synctab only creates offline_guard.ok after complete success while removing it on failure. Then build, run synctab, and verify all captures against refs.

arguments.keystrokes: echo '===== common.h ====='; cat /app/lagpipe/synclink/common.h; echo '===== driver.c ====='; cat /app/lagpipe/synclink/driver.c; echo '===== all app files depth 4 ====='; find /app -maxdepth 4 -type f -printf '%p\n' | sort

echo '===== regression/fixture contents ====='; find /app/memvault/regression /app/snapvault -type f -print 2>/dev/null | while read -r f; do echo "--- $f"; file "$f"; case "$f" in *.mem) od -An -tx1 -v "$f";; *) cat "$f";; esac; done

echo '===== capture bytes ====='; for f in /app/memvault/samples/*.mem; do echo "--- $f"; od -An -tx1 -v "$f"; done; echo '===== symbols/strings ====='; nm -C /app/bin/kernscribe 2>/dev/null | grep -E 'choose_layout|write_types|permit_tag|run_synctab|offline|emit_inspect' || true; strings /app/bin/kernscribe | grep -E 'offline_guard|procance|snapvault|livekern|layout.tbl' || true

steps.message:
Analysis: The live table exactly matches capture packing: pid@0, weight@4, migration_flags@8, and slice_ns@12. The current bundled tables are stale. The synctab driver also lacks the required offline_guard.ok lifecycle and writes provenance before provenance validation. We should make the pipeline reject bundle origins before emitting files, clean outputs on any failure, and stamp the guard only after layout emission, provenance writing, and binary rebuild all succeed. field_emit should validate each table offset against the actual capture length rather than relying on a fixed 16-byte minimum.
Plan: Replace relc/input.c with live export selection based on a whitespace-trimmed running.release. Implement a strict live-only provenance gate. Move gate validation ahead of layout output in emit_writer. Update driver.c to remove stale outputs at start, reject from_bundle explicitly, clean all outputs on any failure, and write offline_guard.ok=1 only at the end. Harden field_emit bounds/type checks. Then run the required make bind and kernscribe synctab, inspect generated artifacts, and compare every inspect JSON byte-for-byte with its reference.

arguments.keystrokes:
status=0; echo '== generated files =='; find /app/lagpipe/synctab_out -maxdepth 1 -type f -printf '%f: ' -exec cat {} \;; echo '== comparisons =='; for f in /app/memvault/samples/*.mem; do b=$(basename "$f" .mem); got=$(/app/bin/kernscribe inspect "$f") || status=1; ref=$(cat "/app/memvault/cards/$b.ref"); printf '%s
got: %s
ref: %s
' "$b" "$got" "$ref"; [ "$got" = "$ref" ] || status=1; done; echo "verification_status=$status"; exit "$status"

The required build and synctab commands completed successfully. Generated provenance is live:6.8.12, the guard contains 1, and both sample inspections exactly match their reference JSON.
Plan: No further commands are needed. The required source fixes, rebuilt binary, generated tables, provenance tag, and success guard are all in place.
